arguments: Unsynchronized global operation table allocation may race and assign the same context to multiple callers
message.text: Unsynchronized global operation table allocation may race and assign the same context to multiple callers

properties.metisTriageReason: Verdict: the reported race is contradicted by the partition configuration and SPM evidence showing the crypto partition uses the SFN model and SFN backend has only one thread, so concurrent entry into this allocation path is not established. Evidence: the shared operations table and check/set allocation are in secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:50 and secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:105-112, while secure_fw/partitions/crypto/tfm_crypto.yaml:13 sets the crypto partition model to SFN and secure_fw/spm/core/interrupt.c:259 documents that SFN backend has only one thread/no thread switch. Gap: none.
properties.mitigation: Protect all accesses and updates to the `operations` table with an appropriate mutex/critical section or use atomic state transitions for slot allocation. Ensure release and lookup follow the same synchronization discipline, or document and enforce single-threaded execution at this boundary.
properties.reasoning: The static global `operations` array is used as a shared allocation table, but the check-and-set sequence for `operations[i].in_use` is not protected by any lock, interrupt exclusion, atomic compare-and-swap, or other synchronization visible in this file. In a concurrent secure partition configuration, two callers could both observe the same slot as not in use before either completes the update, leading to the same backend context being handed out to multiple operations or owners. That could corrupt cryptographic operation state, cause cross-caller state confusion, or undermine owner/type checks later. Exploitability depends on whether this code can run concurrently in the target TF-M configuration, which is not established by this file.
